topic: Valence Electrons and Stability of Atoms
key_concepts: Atomic nuclei contain protons and neutrons
Electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus
Valence electrons are electrons in the outermost shell
The period number equals the number of electron shells
The group number equals the number of valence electrons for representative elements
Electron dot diagrams use dots around an element symbol to show valence electrons
Noble gases are stable because they have eight valence electrons
Atoms can achieve stability by donating, accepting, or sharing electrons
Fluorine has seven valence electrons and can accept one electron to become stable
Group IA and IIA elements tend to donate electrons
Group VIA and VIIA elements tend to accept or share electrons
Group VIIIA elements are already stable
